title: Post-Deployment Verification
goal: Prove in production that the release does what it said, catch early-life problems, and hand a runnable service to OPERATE.

processes.title: Post-Deployment Verification
processes.summary: Smoke-check every deployment, verify production against what the release said would be true, run hypercare, and close and hand over to OPERATE.

definition.purpose: Prove in production that the release does what it said, catch early-life problems, and hand a runnable service to OPERATE.
definition.outcome: Smoke passed, predictions checked against production, hypercare exited, release closed with its outcome and accepted by OPERATE.
definition.jtbd: Help me know — with numbers — that the release worked, and finish it cleanly.
exit: Production verification report signed after the soak
Release record closed with its outcome

normal: Close the release & hand over to OPERATE
parallel: Hypercare overlaps the later rings and the soak
flow.stateTransitions: Deployed → Smoke passed → Verified → Hypercare ended → Closed

cases.happyPath: Smoke passes; every prediction met; hypercare quiet; OPERATE accepts.
alternates: Outcome metrics early → handed to EVOLVE for the outcome review
edgeCases: Prediction exceeded but harmless → ADR updated
Condition open at close → carried as a problem
exceptions: Measurement broken → fix and re-read before close

routing.forward: Closed release, runbook, SLOs → OPERATE; retrospective and learning log → EVOLVE
routing.alternate: Early outcome readings → EVOLVE outcome review
routing.rework: Measurement gap → re-read; rejected handover → fill the gaps
routing.escalation: Smoke fails or prediction badly missed → release manager; Sev-1/2 → incident command
routing.stop: Production check failed → roll back; release closed as failed — recorded in the learning log

rules: No release closed without a production check
Mismatches become defects, problems or ADR updates
policies: Flags removed on a scheduled date

decisions: Did production match what we said? Does OPERATE accept?

roles: R — SRE, Support lead, Engineering lead
execution.authority: Release manager judges the production check and closes the release; the operations lead accepts the service.

continuity.handoff: Closed release record, operational handover, runbook and SLOs → OPERATE; release retrospective → EVOLVE
traceability: Creates PDV-### linking DEP, RING, NFR and ADR IDs; closes RC, CHG and GNG
continuity.timebox: Smoke in minutes; soak 72 hours at full exposure; hypercare up to two weeks
measures: Days from full exposure to close
learning: Release retrospective; predictions that were wrong — learning log

loops: Production check failed → closed as failed

lessons.title: Run Smoke Checks
lessons.summary: Prove immediately after each deployment that the critical path and the fallback work in production, then keep synthetic checks running.

definition.purpose: Prove right after each deployment that the critical path works in production before anyone is exposed.
definition.outcome: Smoke and synthetic checks passed and recorded for the deployment.
definition.jtbd: Help me know within minutes whether the deployment works at all.

normal: Smoke the critical path and the fallback
dependencies: Test inbox and ERP sandbox tenant
flow.stateTransitions: Deployed → Smoke running → Passed / Failed → Synthetic running

cases.happyPath: 5 of 5 smoke checks pass in three minutes.
alternates: Flag-only change → smoke the flag paths
edgeCases: Smoke needs production data → use a test tenant, never real orders
exceptions: Flaky check → re-run once, then treat as a failure

routing.alternate: Flag-off release → smoke the fallback path only
routing.rework: Flaky → fix the check and re-run
routing.stop: Rolled back → release paused — recorded in the learning log

criteria: Critical path and fallback both exercised
rules: Smoke never uses real customer data
policies: Synthetic checks stay on after the release

standards: ISO/IEC 20000-1 — verify before and after deployment
methods: Guardrail metrics — baseline readings at deployment

concerns: A broken deployment exposed to users

execution.authority: Release manager decides on rollback when smoke fails.

workflows.title: Run the Smoke Checks
workflows.summary: Right after deployment, run health checks and smoke the critical path and the fallback with test data, then start continuous synthetic checks.

lenses.note: Test tenant only — no real customer data.

uses.name: Guardrail metrics — baseline readings at deployment

contract.handoff: Smoke check results → 6.3.2 Run Ring 0 and 6.5.2 Verify Production Against Predictions

lessons.exercise: On your own project, produce Smoke check results and Synthetic check results — so that: Smoke and synthetic checks passed and recorded for the deployment.
lessons.prompt:
I'm working through "Run Smoke Checks" (Release → Post-Deployment Verification) on my own project. Act as my assistant: draft and check, I decide.

Goal: Prove right after each deployment that the critical path works in production before anyone is exposed.
Done looks like: Smoke and synthetic checks passed and recorded for the deployment.

I'll attach or paste: Deployment record; Release test evidence.

Work through these steps with me, one at a time:
1. Run health checks
2. Smoke critical path & fallback → Smoke check results
3. All passed? (a decision — give me the options and a recommendation; I make the call)
4. Start synthetic checks → Synthetic check results
5. Record results → Smoke check results

Produce: Smoke check results; Synthetic check results. Use clear headings I can paste into my document.

Before you finish, check it against: Critical path and fallback both exercised; Critical path and fallback pass.

Ask me for anything you need instead of guessing. Keep it specific to my project.

lessons.title: Run Hypercare
lessons.summary: Give the first weeks of live use extra attention — daily check-ins, fast triage, the building team on hand — and exit on criteria.

definition.purpose: Give the first weeks of live use extra attention so early-life problems are caught and fixed fast.
definition.outcome: A hypercare log, early-life defects routed, and an exit agreed against criteria.
definition.jtbd: Help me catch what shows up only when real people use it every day.
exit: Every early-life defect routed with an owner

parallel: Per-site hypercare overlaps as rings are promoted
flow.stateTransitions: Started → Daily → Exit criteria met → Ended

cases.happyPath: Tickets fall to normal in five days; no Sev-1/2.
edgeCases: Lyon tickets spike after its ring
Cause outside the release (scanner settings at a site)
exceptions: A defect needs a hotfix → roll forward through a new change
failures: Hypercare ends by date, not by criteria

routing.forward: Hypercare log & early-life defects → 6.5.4 Close & Hand Over; problems → OPERATE problem backlog
routing.alternate: Short hypercare for a low-risk change
routing.rework: Not yet at exit criteria → continue
routing.stop: Release withdrawn → hypercare ends with the rollback — recorded in the learning log

rules: Every defect routed to the backlog with severity and owner
policies: The building team stays on hand during hypercare

execution.authority: Support lead exits hypercare against its criteria; the release manager agrees.

continuity.handoff: Hypercare log → 6.5.4; problems → OPERATE problem backlog
traceability: Early-life DEF-### and PRB-### linked to RC-###
continuity.timebox: Up to two weeks per site

workflows.title: Run Hypercare
workflows.summary: Hold a daily check-in, triage tickets and defects, route each to the backlog with an owner, keep the help content current, and exit only on the agreed criteria.

lenses.note: Daily check-in with sites and engineers.
Tickets read for what users are really struggling with.
Problems routed to OPERATE's problem backlog.
Exit on criteria, not on the calendar.

contract.definition: Hold a daily check-in, triage tickets and defects, route each to the backlog with an owner, keep the help content current, and exit only on the agreed criteria.
decisions: Are the hypercare exit criteria met?
recovery: Route each with severity and owner
contract.rework: Criteria not met → another day of hypercare
contract.handoff: Hypercare log → 6.5.4 Close the Release & Hand Over; problem records → OPERATE problem backlog
traceability: Early-life DEF-### and PRB-### linked to RC-###

lessons.exercise: On your own project, produce Hypercare log and Early-life defect list and Problem record — so that: A hypercare log, early-life defects routed, and an exit agreed against criteria.
lessons.prompt:

Goal: Give the first weeks of live use extra attention so early-life problems are caught and fixed fast.

lessons.title: Close the Release & Hand Over to OPERATE
lessons.summary: Close the release with its outcome recorded, schedule flag removal, and hand a runnable service to OPERATE, accepted on evidence.

definition.purpose: Close the release with its outcome recorded and hand a runnable service to OPERATE, accepted on evidence.
definition.outcome: A closed release record, flags scheduled for removal, the operational handover accepted and learning captured.
definition.jtbd: Help me finish cleanly, so OPERATE owns a service it can run and we know how the release went.
entry: Hypercare exited, or handed over with it
exit: Release record closed with its outcome

cases.happyPath: Operations accepts; release closed 'passed with issues'.
edgeCases: A condition still open at close → carried as a problem with an owner
exceptions: SLOs not yet agreed → interim targets with a date
failures: Release never closed — it drifts open

routing.forward: Release record, operational handover, runbook and SLOs → OPERATE (Act VII); release retrospective & learning log → EVOLVE
routing.rework: Operations rejects → fill the gaps and re-present
routing.stop: Rolled-back release → closed as failed with its problem record — recorded in the learning log

criteria: Outcome recorded, including what went wrong
checks: Every flag has a removal date and a backlog item
rules: Closed only after the production check and soak
Change record closed with its outcome

execution.authority: Operations lead accepts the service; the release manager closes the release.

continuity.handoff: Release record, operational handover pack, runbook and SLOs → OPERATE; retrospective and learning log → EVOLVE
traceability: Closes RC, CHG and GNG; creates LRN-### linked to RC-###
continuity.timebox: ½ day handover; retrospective within a week of close
measures: Days from full exposure to close

workflows.title: Close the Release & Hand Over
